cards.title: Broth Microdilution Method and MIC Definition
cards.claim: For an agent-organism pair for which broth microdilution is the qualified reference method, record the MIC as the lowest antimicrobial concentration meeting the applicable growth-inhibition endpoint, expressed in mg/L or µg/mL. The standard endpoint is complete visible-growth inhibition; method and endpoint applicability must be verified before use.
conditions: Use MH-F broth (Mueller-Hinton broth + 5% lysed horse blood + 20 mg/L β-NAD) for fastidious organisms.
Standard MH broth for non-fastidious organisms.
Results must be recorded as MIC values, not just categorical susceptibility.
required_inputs: Microorganism identity and the qualified assay method for the agent-organism pair.
Broth composition, incubation protocol and endpoint definition with method/version provenance.
limitations: Broth microdilution and complete-inhibition reading are not universal for every agent-organism pair.
Specific exceptions must be checked in the applicable assay protocol; this generic card does not prescribe those drug-specific procedures.
Text extraction does not verify visual growth patterns; requires trained manual or calibrated automated reading.
cards.downstream_use: Defines the fundamental data type (MIC in mg/L) and experimental conditions required for PK/PD modeling inputs.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
